Pallet and Carton Flow Racking

Flow racking uses gently inclined roller lanes so that pallets or cartons loaded at the back move by gravity to the picking face at the front. It gives strict first-in, first-out stock rotation and separates replenishment from picking.

How it works

How pallet and carton flow racking works

Each lane is a slightly inclined bed of rollers. Pallets or cartons are loaded at the upper end and roll forward until they reach the front, where they are picked. When one is removed, the next moves forward.

Brake rollers control the speed of loaded pallets, and separators at the picking end take the pressure of the lane off the front pallet so it can be lifted safely.

Is it the right fit?

When to choose pallet and carton flow racking

  • Products have expiry dates or batches
  • You need strict FIFO without extra handling
  • You want to separate loading from picking
  • Picking speed is critical

Compare

When another system may fit better

  • Drive-through racking for dense FIFO block storage at lower cost.
  • Multi-tier shelving for manual picking of small items.
  • Selective pallet racking when every pallet must be accessible.

Questions

Pallet and Carton Flow Racking FAQs

How does pallet flow racking work?

Pallets are loaded at the back of an inclined roller lane and move forward by gravity to the picking face. Brake rollers control the speed and separators at the front protect the operator when the first pallet is removed.

What is the difference between pallet flow and carton flow racking?

Pallet flow racking moves full pallets for bulk picking or dispatch. Carton flow racking uses lighter roller or wheel lanes for cartons and totes, usually at waist height for fast manual order picking.

What are the requirements for flow racking to work reliably?

Flow lanes need pallets or cartons of consistent size, weight and base quality, because damaged or irregular pallets can stop in the lane. Load details are reviewed during design so the rollers and brakes suit the actual goods.
